sentence: This project builds and tests a technology that locates and images the epileptogenic brain in patients with drug resistant focal epilepsy, without invasive methods.
This project tests whether an AI model using stethoscope sound files can screen dialysis patients for stenosis in an arteriovenous fistula.
This project develops and checks biomarkers from imaging and biofluids to predict disease risk, and uses mass spectrometric approaches to find more biomarkers.
This project covers the statistical and mathematical details behind analyzing data from single-cell technologies that study thousands of individual cells.
This project adds a service-learning design course, a summer clinical immersion with local hospitals and a medical device commercialization workshop to a biomedical engineering program.
This project tests whether radiation can be used as the energy for ablation to treat ventricular tachycardia in a non-invasive way.
This project tries to find small molecules that switch on gasdermin pores so tumor cells die and the immune system attacks the cancer.
This project tests whether Duoseq, which sequences DNA and RNA together, can diagnose lymphomas faster and more cheaply than current methods.
This project tries to find and remove an extremely active transposable element in an inbred mouse strain, using computational tools.
This project studies how the fruit fly senses and responds to the dead of its own kind, and what drives that response.
This project measures chromatin accessibility and RNA expression together in single cells to map gene regulatory networks and cell states.
This project develops magnetic resonance imaging techniques to assess tissue injury and survival in a mouse model of neonatal hypoxic ischemic injury.
This project builds computer methods that make genetic predictions of behavioral traits and link data from the gut, vagus, and brain.
This project studies how phosphorylation changes the way the heart proteins titin and myosin work, and how that goes wrong in heart failure.
This project brings engineering and clinical neuroscience together to image, analyze, and modulate activity in neural circuits for disorders of the nervous system.
This project studies how glioblastoma, a brain tumor, avoids the immune system, and develops a treatment strategy based on that.
This project covers plant biotechnology, drawing on plant biology, biochemistry, metabolic engineering, synthetic biology and computational biology.
This project studies how a protease called Lon helps the bacterium Acinetobacter baumannii survive desiccation and cause disease.
This project studies how social and physical environments and loneliness are linked to cognition in older people with HIV.
This project builds a tool that labels proteins in specific tissues of Drosophila to study how disease-related proteins behave over time and space.
